platform.description: The client platform the widget will render on. Pass 'mobile' when your system prompt indicates a mobile client (narrow ~380px viewport) so SVG viewBox and layout guidance are sized accordingly; otherwise pass 'desktop'. Defaults to 'unknown' (desktop sizing).

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

entries.name: mcp__ccd_host__sync_with_base_branch
entries.description:
Bring this session's branch up to date with its base branch: the app fetches the base from `origin` and merges it into the branch checked out in this session's worktree, running git on the host, outside your sandbox, which cannot write the repository's protected paths (`.claude/hooks`, `.claude/skills`, `.mcp.json` and the like) that such a merge often touches. Use it instead of `git merge`/`git pull` whenever you need the base branch's latest commits, e.g. to resolve a pull request's merge conflicts.

`base` defaults to the base the app knows for this session (its open pull request's base, else the branch the worktree was cut from); you may name that branch or the repository's default branch, nothing else. A session that also holds a worktree for an extra folder of another repository merges into the worktree your current directory is in, or the one `folder` names (either path the workspace note shows for that folder, or the folder's last segment when only one of the session's folders ends in it); the base is then that repository's. Sandbox-protected files are brought in only from the repository's default branch; any other base merges only when it leaves those files alone, and a protected file both this branch and the base changed is left for a person (the call refuses). Nothing is pushed. Outcomes: merged (a merge commit or fast-forward; run the project's checks, then push), up to date, or conflicts: the merge is then left in progress with the conflicted files listed for you to resolve, `git add` and `git commit --no-edit` (protected files this branch only had an older upstream copy of are already taken from the base). `abort: true` abandons a merge left in progress instead. It refuses rather than touch uncommitted changes, another git operation in progress, files the repository routes through a content filter (git-lfs, git-crypt), a fork checkout whose origin is not the pull request's repository, or a session without its own worktree; merge yourself in those cases. In default mode the user approves each call on a card; in auto mode the app's classifier decides.

base.description: The base branch to merge, when the session's own isn't the one you need: its pull request's base, the branch the worktree was cut from, or the repository's default branch.

abort.description: true to abandon a merge this tool left in progress (git merge --abort) instead of merging.

folder.description: Which of this session's worktrees to act on, when it holds one for an extra folder of another repository: either path the workspace note shows for that folder, or its last segment when only one of the session's folders ends in it; the session's own folder names its own worktree. Default: the worktree your current directory is in, else the session's own.

_consent.description: Set by the app. Never set this yourself.

The frontend is running at **http://localhost:5176**, with your branch up to date with `origin/main` (5 new commits, including the landing-page update from PR #16).

- **Port:** 5173–5175 were already in use, probably by dev servers in other worktrees, so Vite moved to 5176. That only matters for Google sign-in, because Supabase's redirect list has `localhost:5173` in it.
- **No `.env`:** there isn't one in this worktree or the main checkout, so the app runs on sample data with sign-in turned off. To sign in, copy `frontend/.env.example` to `frontend/.env` and fill in the two Supabase values.
- **Checked:** the landing page at `/` and the dashboard at `/home` (logged in as "Demo researcher") both load with no console errors.
- **AGENTS.md is out of date:** it describes `frontend/` as **Motus**, a tool for monitoring ALS at home through speech and typing. The app it runs is now **Addo Labs**, an ALS drug discovery tool. AGENTS.md says to fix this kind of mismatch right away, since every agent working in the repo reads that file.

`npm install` also reported 6 vulnerabilities (2 low, 4 moderate). I didn't look into them.

#15 Motus: 15 dashboard views are still placeholders [track:frontend] assignees=
Only Overview is built. The rest render 'coming soon' copy from `VIEWS` in
`frontend/src/pages/Home.tsx`. Fine for a demo that only opens Overview —
decide which, if any, matter before Sunday.
======
#14 Decide demo mode: signed-in or sample data [track:frontend,decision] assignees=
Sample data works today with no keys and shows a Sample data badge. Sign-in
needs Supabase keys in `frontend/.env` (see `.env.example`).
======
#13 Three knowledge graphs exist — pick one [track:frontend,decision] assignees=
Neo's `GraphCanvas`, Henri's stale `KnowledgeGraph.tsx`, and a 'coming soon'
placeholder on `main`.
======
#12 Decide: FaceCheck as its own page, or a tab [track:facecheck,decision] assignees=
`docs/FACECHECK_SPEC.md` §7. Also: two FaceChecks exist — Neo's TS original and
Levi's JS port. Pick one.
======
#11 Write docs/SPEECH_SPEC.md [track:speech] assignees=
The only track with no spec. Two branches of work nobody else can pick up or
pitch. Same shape as `FACECHECK_SPEC.md`: what it's for, what exists, what's
open, what's unverified.
======
#10 Port the Python pipeline onto a branch cut from main [track:pipeline] assignees=
`main` has no pipeline code. `cursor/pipeline-graph-ui` has it, but also edits
`app/`, which main deleted — 11 conflicts, 9 of them that.

Clean approach, no conflicts:

```bash
git checkout -b pipeline/python origin/main
git checkout origin/cursor/pipeline-graph-ui -- \
  bbb_model.py patient_filter.py merge.py graveyard.py \
  requirements.txt bbb/ src/ tests/ scripts/ server/
```

Leave `data/*.json` and `artifacts/` behind — gitignored now, and that branch's
`pipeline.json` is 10.5 MB against main's 200 KB.
======
#9 Wire real DRKG vectors into discovery stage 3 [track:discovery] assignees=
`MATCHES` in `frontend/src/lib/pipeline.ts` is hand-written. Neo's `src/drkg.py`
loads the real TransE vectors.

DRKG embeds *entities*, not text — a profile needs to become DRKG genes before
it has a vector. Jeremy's `PROFILES` already list target genes, so: map to
`Gene::<Entrez>`, average, cosine against compound vectors. Short bridge.
======
#8 Stop saying 24 never-arrived drugs — it is 3 [track:discovery,blocker] assignees=
Measured against Neo's real `pipeline.json`:

24 `never_arrived` / 8 `arrived_failed`, but **21 of the 24 have no BBB
prediction at all** (biologics, or out of the model's domain). `src/merge.py:211-214`
files 'no prediction' as `never_arrived`.

Only ceftriaxone (0.39), pentoxifylline (0.29) and pioglitazone (0.29) are
actually predicted BBB-negative. Honest split: **3 / 8 / 21 undetermined.**

Same error in the funnel: '2,440 predicted BBB-negative' is 1,593 predicted +
847 out of domain.

**Use 1,593 of 3,791** — still the strong number, and it survives a question.
A judge who knows gabapentin crosses the BBB will catch the other one.
======
#7 Jeremy and Levi are building the same five agents [track:discovery,decision,blocker] assignees=
**Jeremy:** five-stage pipeline in `frontend/`, scripted TypeScript, `MATCHES`
hand-written, labelled Simulated.

**Levi:** `backend/query-generation/` on `agentic-query-generation` — five real
Python agents (disease-indications, genes-targets, pathways-processes,
safety-interactions-class, symptoms-function) plus rank intersection and a
fallback policy, grounded in DRKG.

Same five agents, twice. **No shared git history** — no merge base with `main`.

Cheapest win in the repo: make Jeremy's `PipelineEvent` stream come from Levi's
agents instead of a timer. His module header already says a live backend only
has to emit the same events. The trees never have to meet — JSON over the seam.
======
#6 Pick the name: Addo Labs or motus [decision,blocker] assignees=
`frontend/src/lib/theme.ts`, `lib/pipeline.ts` and `discovery/report.tsx` say
**Addo Labs**. The landing page says **motus**. A judge sees both in one scroll.
======
#5 Pick the product: discovery pipeline or Motus [decision,blocker] assignees=
Both ship on `main`, in one sidebar, sharing nothing else.

A judge gets 90 seconds and can follow one argument. Everything else is
downstream of this call.

See `docs/DISCOVERY_SPEC.md` §4.
======

content.content:
means **the honest claim is "here is the system we designed", not "here is
a system that found these drugs".** The sample patient (`A-0417`, bulbar
onset, 14 months, ALSFRS 38, Toronto/OHIP, `fusEligible: true`) and its
candidates are hand-written.

A live backend only has to emit the same `PipelineEvent`s. That's a clean
seam; don't let anyone collapse it under time pressure.

---

## 4. Open questions — these need people, not agents

1. **Is this the product, or is Motus?** `main` currently ships a landing
   page and a longitudinal monitoring dashboard (speech/typing/handwriting
   vs personal baseline) *and* this discovery pipeline. They share a sidebar
   and nothing else. One demo, 90 seconds — a judge can follow one argument.
   **This is the most important open question in the repo.**
2. **What is it called?** `theme.ts`, `pipeline.ts` and `report.tsx` say
   **Addo Labs**. The landing page says **motus**. Pick one today.
3. **Does the old elimination funnel feed this?** The discovery module is
   self-contained and never reads `data/pipeline.json`. Either wire the
   graveyard in as the candidate pool (§1 — cheap, and it makes the two
   tracks one story) or retire the contract and say so.
4. **Answered → [`FUS_RESEARCH.md`](FUS_RESEARCH.md).** Was: **Can we cite the Sunnybrook FUS work accurately?** The claim rests on
   it. Get real citations for BBB opening in ALS or in neurodegeneration
   generally, and be precise about what has been shown in humans versus what
   is proposed. Mark anything unverified as unverified — a judge who knows
   the field will ask.
5. **Does FaceCheck still fit?** See `FACECHECK_SPEC.md` §7.

---

## 5. Risks worth naming before a judge does

- **Safety inverts too.** Opening the BBB for a drug also opens it for
  everything else circulating, and the drugs this unlocks were often not
  designed for CNS exposure. "It can now get in" is not "it is now safe
  once it's in." Having an answer here is a strength.
- **The ranking is the claim.** Cosine similarity in DRKG plus an LLM's
  reading is a hypothesis generator, not evidence. Frame the output as "what
  to investigate next", never as a recommendation.
======
# Decisions

Append-only, newest first. Three lines each: **what** we decided, **why**,
and what it **rules out**.

A decision here is settled — don't re-litigate it without new information.
If you reverse one, append the reversal; don't edit the old entry away.

---

## 2026-11-08 — Research sub-agents describe drugs, they don't name them

**What:** `agent/` sub-agents return target profiles (HGNC targets + desired
action, pathways, site, constraints, evidence) and never drug names; a
separate matcher (DRKG / embeddings) turns profiles into drugs.
**Why:** an LLM naming drugs pre-empts and biases the matching step, and
lands on the same famous handful every time. Profiles are also what Levi's
DRKG agents need as anchors.
**Rules out:** sub-agents with drug-level tools, or drug names in profile
text (`no_drugs.py` scrubs them). Drug-level tools stay for the matcher.

## 2026-11-07 — `frontend/` (Motus) is the only frontend

**What:** Deleted `app/` (Vite drug-funnel UI) and `web/` (a Next 16 rebuild
of the same). `frontend/` is the one frontend.
**Why:** Three frontends existed for one project because nobody checked
before starting. Two of them rendered a story we are no longer leading with.
**Rules out:** Reviving the lab-console funnel UI as-is. It's in git history
(`6c9a0f4` and parents) if any of it is wanted back.

## 2026-11-07 — The contract lives in `contract/`, not inside a frontend

**What:** Moved `contract.ts`, `contract.test.ts` and `validate.ts` out of
`app/src/lib/` into a standalone `contract/` package with one dependency
(zod).
**Why:** The Python owners run `npm run validate` to check their output. That
check must not die because a frontend was deleted, and it must not require
installing React to run.
**Rules out:** Putting schema code inside any app directory again.

content.text:
I've updated AGENTS.md, but not by just swapping in the new name. Issues #5 (which product) and #6 (which name) are both still open and marked as blockers, so writing "Addo Labs" in as settled would have made those calls for the team. The file now says what `main` ships today (Addo Labs, with Motus as its "Patient monitoring" view) and that the name and product are still open in #5 and #6. I left README.md alone because it's the Motus pitch, and replacing it is part of the #5 decision.

## Other decisions still open

All are unassigned. With 9:00 am as the real deadline, the first three set the pitch.

1. **#5 Product: discovery pipeline or Motus.** Every other decision depends on this one. The code has already leaned one way: PR #16 made the landing page say "ALS drug discovery optimization", the sidebar starts with pipeline stages 00–05, and Motus is now one page under Library. Someone needs to approve that (add a line to `docs/DECISIONS.md` and close the issue) or reverse it.
2. **#6 Name.** What the issue says is no longer true: the landing page now says "addo labs" too. Every file in `frontend/` says Addo Labs; only the README and older docs still say Motus. It just needs someone to approve it.
3. **#7 Jeremy and Levi are both building the same five agents.** The issue suggests the cheapest fix: Levi's Python agents produce the `PipelineEvent`s that Jeremy's UI currently fakes on a timer.
4. **#14 Demo mode.** I found no `.env` here or in your main checkout, so in practice the demo runs on sample data. Google sign-in would also need port 5173 free, and it's taken on your machine right now.
5. **#13 Knowledge graph.** There are three versions; pick one, or hide the "Knowledge graph" page.
6. **#15 Placeholder pages.** 15 pages show "coming soon". Decide which ones to hide before judges click on them.
7. **#12 FaceCheck as its own page or a tab.** If #5 goes to the discovery pipeline, this probably becomes "drop it".
8. **Does the drug funnel feed discovery, or do we retire the contract?** This is open question 3 in `docs/DISCOVERY_SPEC.md`, and **no issue tracks it**. The discovery pipeline never reads `data/pipeline.json`, so either connect it (the spec calls this cheap, and it ties the two tracks into one story) or say the contract is retired.
9. **Merging `Master-UI-Neo-Face-Integration`.** AGENTS.md says merging this branch is a decision. It's probably moot if #5 goes to the discovery pipeline.

**#8 isn't a decision, but it matters for the pitch.** "24 drugs never reached the brain" is wrong: it's 3 predicted BBB-negative, 8 that arrived and failed, and 21 undetermined. The safe number to quote is **1,593 of 3,791**.
